events.title: 2026 SUPPLY CHAIN CONSULTING LECTURE SERIES
events.description: PURDUE STUDENTS ARE INVITED Students across Purdue majors and programs are warmly invited to attend any or all sessions. Join us to learn directly from industry professionals, ask questions, explore career paths, and connect classroom ideas with real-world supply chain and consulting practice. ABOUT THE SERIES The 2026 Supply Chain Consulting Lecture Series connects Purdue students with experienced supply chain executives, consultants, alumni, and industry professionals to explore how organizations solve complex supply chain and operations challenges in practice. The series is an integral part of SCOM 469 — Supply Chain and Operations Analytics Consulting, a 3-credit experiential learning course that transforms the classroom into a professional consulting environment. Student teams apply supply chain theory, data analytics, AI-enabled tools, and structured consulting methods to real-world business and industry challenges. THE THREE-PILLAR EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING MODEL Consulting & Industry Study Projects — Students learn by solving real business and industry problems through corporate-sponsored consulting engagements and advisor-guided industry studies.Mentoring Program — Experienced alumni and industry professionals coach student teams on problem solving, analytics, project management, executive storytelling, and professional development. Jeffrey R. Powers, retired IBM executive and Purdue alumnus, chairs the Industry Advisory Board.Industry Lecture Series — Practitioners bring current challenges, emerging technologies, leadership lessons, and real-world decision making directly into the classroom. SCOM 469 builds on Purdue’s university–industry partnerships and experiential projects with organizations including Wabash, Rolls-Royce, Corteva, Taste, and other corporate and industry partners. For Fall 2026, students will work through two experiential project pathways: the corporate project Taste Omnichannel Dining Service Optimization and the industry study Enhancing Pharmaceutical Supply-Chain Resilience. WHY ATTEND? Learn from experienced professionals — See how practitioners approach ambiguous, high-impact supply chain problems.Understand professional practice — Explore consulting, leadership, sourcing, planning, program management, and digital transformation in action.Connect analytics and AI to execution — See how data, analytics, and AI shape consulting strategy and day-to-day supply chain decisions.Connect classroom frameworks to real decisions — Examine constraints, cross-functional trade-offs, and the realities of implementation.Build your professional network — Meet Purdue alumni and experienced industry professionals while exploring supply chain career paths.All Purdue students are welcome. You do not need to be enrolled in SCOM 469 to participate. Attend the sessions that match your interests, come prepared to ask questions and share perspectives, and use the series as an opportunity to learn and build professional connections. FALL 2026 LECTURE SCHEDULE SEPTEMBER 3 — Consulting 101 Isaac Tipton — CEO, Prowire USA The opening session introduces the foundations of consulting and structured problem solving. Drawing on professional experience, the speakers will discuss how consultants approach ambiguous business problems, work with clients and teams, communicate insights, and translate analysis into actionable recommendations. SEPTEMBER 17 — Program Management in Supply Chain: From Plan to Execution Michelle Kozlowski — Senior Program Manager, Amazon Catherine “Cathy” Nash — Sales & Operations Execution Planner, Constellation Brands Strong strategies create value only when organizations can execute them. This session focuses on program management, planning, coordination, accountability, and execution—examining how supply chain professionals move from plans and priorities to operational results across people, processes, and functions. OCTOBER 1 — Trade-Off Management + Cross-Functional Procurement & Sourcing Decisions Amanda Tronchin — Finance & Strategy Consultant, Pinnacle Strategy Group Eduardo Da Silva-Witzke — Aftermarket Sourcing Analyst, Cummins Inc. Supply chain and procurement decisions frequently require balancing competing objectives across cost, service, risk, quality, capacity, and strategic priorities. This session explores how professionals structure trade-offs, collaborate across functions, and translate financial, operational, and strategic considerations into sourcing and procurement decisions. OCTOBER 15 — Leadership, Influence & the Human Side of Supply Chain Consulting Kriti Gupta — Director of Operations, Amazon Nilo Cedeno-Guadamud — Global Category Manager, Wabash Analytics alone rarely produces organizational change. This session explores the human side of supply chain leadership and consulting—including stakeholder influence, relationship building, communication, team leadership, negotiation, and the ability to move organizations from insight to action. OCTOBER 29 — AI in Supply Chain: From Consulting Strategy to Everyday Execution Vishal Madisetti — Associate, Emerging Platforms, KPMG US Brookelle Mathieson — Life Sciences Supply Chain Management Consultant, Accenture Possible contributor: Khushi Karmokar — Procurement Analyst, ThoughtSpot AI is changing both how consultants solve problems and how supply chain professionals perform everyday work. This session explores practical applications of AI, analytics, automation, and emerging technologies—from consulting strategy and transformation initiatives to operational decision support, procurement, and day-to-day execution. NOVEMBER 12 — Planning, Constraints & Supply Chain Systems Thinking Kyle Harshbarger — Supply Chain Engineer, Marathon Petroleum Lauren Heiss — Senior Technology Consultant, EY The final session brings together planning, constraints, technology, and systems thinking. The speakers will connect MRP/ERP concepts, bottlenecks, lessons from The Goal, and real-world planning challenges to the broader question of how supply chains operate as interconnected systems. The session will also explore supply chain career paths and how the strategic role of the supply chain function varies across industries. CONNECTING INDUSTRY AND THE CLASSROOM The Industry Lecture Series is not designed as a collection of stand-alone guest presentations. Each session is integrated with students’ consulting and industry-study work. Student teams are encouraged to bring questions from their projects into the classroom, apply lessons from speakers to their analyses, and reflect on how different professionals approach similar challenges across industries. Student ambassadors will also work directly with speakers before selected sessions to help prepare and contextualize the lectures, providing another opportunity to develop professional communication, stakeholder-management, and networking skills. Theory → Evidence → Insight → Recommendation → Impact HOSTED BY Zhan Pang Professor of Supply Chain and Operations Management Instructor, SCOM 469 — Supply Chain and Operations Analytics Consulting Purdue University REGISTER FOR SESSION UPDATES https://purdue.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_2fB3x8h9fODi52S Questions? events.title: Executive Forum with Vivek Chakrabortty, Chief Executive Officer for The Kavi Group LLC
events.description: The Executive Forum is open to the public, as seating permits, and provides opportunities for the exchange of ideas and discussion of topics and issues facing business and management. Vivek was born in Mumbai, India, in a Brahmin Hindu and Catholic household and grew up in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, a Muslim country. One grandfather was an Indian Freedom Fighter, and the other was in the British Navy. From a very young age, my parents instilled an empathetic, diverse way of thinking in Vivek and his brother. His love for travel and desire to know people with different backgrounds and life stories is rooted in his own diversity. You could say he has been a risk taker and entrepreneur his whole life. He grew up in the rigorous and structured CBSE Indian school system where you had to choose between science, commerce, or arts at the age of 16. He craved freedom and knew that a path in America would enable him to be whomever he wanted to be. He negotiated with his dad to attend high school and college in the US, and moved when he was just 16. His life forever changed. It was only by chance that he started to work in operations resilience before two major US events happened: 9/11 and Hurricane Katrina. As a business continuity and crisis management consultant, he learned that businesses must be one step ahead of the threats faced by their clients whether they are natural disasters, civic unrest, terrorism, active shooters, cyber-security breaches, technology failures, or catastrophic accidents. He was the emergency preparedness advisor to the Louisiana Recovery Authority in the aftermath of hurricanes Katrina and Rita and led the California Healthcare Surge Planning which was the first of its kind in the U.S. in terms of scale and scope. The teams he led on these two projects were awarded the Chairman’s Award, PwC’s highest recognition for outstanding client service. In the past 25 years, he has worked in the American South, Northeast, Midwest, Pacific Northwest, California, and Mid-Atlantic. His work has taken him to Europe, Australia, and Asia. These experiences as well as his understanding of culture and people prepared him to be an entrepreneur. In 2014, his wife Kathy and Vivek invested their life savings to start the Kavi Group, a management consulting firm that provides business continuity and crisis management advisory services. Today, Kavi Group is a 7-figure company with Fortune 100 companies as their clients. Kavi has helped our clients navigate the COVID19 pandemic, supply chain risks and disruptions, geo-political conflicts, climate-change associated threats, and adjust to the new normal of risk management.

events.title: AAARCC Scholar in Residence: Sharing History & Heritage through Mahjong with Jennie Mak
events.description: The AAARCC hosts an artist and scholar in residence each semester to highlight national and local experts in weaving narratives, leading communities, and engaging future generations. Join us in-person at the AAARCC (915 5th St) and virtually on Tuesday, November 3, and Wednesday, November 4, for presentations, workshops, and open play sessions to discuss "Sharing History & Heritage through Mahjong" with Jennie Mak. No mahjong experience is necessary to participate. The Fall 2026 Scholar in Residence Program is partially funded by SFAB. Flyer: https://aaarcc.short.gy/mahjong About Jennie Mak Jennie Mak is the founder of Mahjong United, a community project in Washington, DC born from her love of teaching and storytelling through mahjong. Raised in a mahjong-playing household in Hong Kong and graduated from Purdue University with a Bachelor's degree in Psychology, she now teaches both kids and adults, using the game to connect generations and celebrate culture. Jennie sees beauty in every style—Hong Kong, American, Riichi, Filipino, Siamese— and views mahjong as a bridge between generations, cultures, and conversations. Lunch & Learn: Life Lessons from the Mahjong Table Tuesday, November 3 | 12:00 PM – 1:00 PM | AAARCC (915 5th St.) and Virtual over Microsoft Teams Get your introduction to mahjong and Jennie Mak's work with Mahjong United in Washington, DC. This event will discuss how mahjong can be used to cultivate life skills as we navigate identity, language, cultural inheritance, conflict, and belonging. Cannot join in-person? Register to join the livestream through Microsoft Teams: https://aaarcc.short.gy/mahjongtalk Crafting Workshop: Mahjong Tiles as Cultural Heritage Tuesday, November 3 | 3PM – 5 PM | AAARCC (915 5th St.) The craft of carving mahjong tile sets has been recognized as as an Intangible Cultural Heritage. Design your own keepsake tile and create a "House Rules" zine while learning about the traditional visual motifs found in mahjong-playing cultures. Materials provided in partnership with the Weldon School of Biomedical Engineering. From a Table of Four to 150: Building Community Through Play Tuesday, November 3 | 5:30PM – 6:30 PM | AAARCC (915 5th St.) What turns a gathering into a community? Learn how mahjong event pop-ups are bridging generations, cultures, and conversations. Explore how student-led initiatives, such as Purdue Mahjong Club, has used mahjong to build community, exchange knowledge, and grow sense of belonging right here on campus. Refreshments will be provided. Forty-plus Ways to Play Mahjong Wednesday, November 4 | AAARCC (915 5th St.) Morning Session: 10:30AM-12:00PM Afternoon Session: 2:00PM-3:00PM Take a break and enjoy a cup of coffee or tea while playing different variations of mahjong! Beginners can learn how to play Hong Kong style mahjong with Jennie. Tables for other mahjong play-styles and skill levels will be available and we look forward for attendees to exchange stories, game rules, strategies, and scoring systems. Table Talk: Connecting Communities, Honoring Heritage, & Inspiring Conversation Wednesday, November 4 | 5:30PM – 7:00 PM | AAARCC (915 5th St.) Curious about the role of Purdue alumni have in sharing the mahjong game with American communities? Join mahjong scholars and practitioners Jennie Mak and Nicole Wong for a discussion of a broader histories of heritage, migration, and belonging that mahjong carries, from the 1900s to now. Cannot join in-person? Register to join the livestream through Microsoft Teams: https://aaarcc.short.gy/tabletalk Virtual Panelist: Nichole Wong is writer and audio producer based in Oakland, California. Her parents immigrated from New Zealand in the 1980s to Santa Monica, California. While cleaning out their garage, they rediscovered the mahjong table they’d brought over with them along with a few extra sets of tiles and the memories from playing with her grandparents in the Auckland summers. She started The Mahjong Project book and online guide in 2019 to document her family’s house rules for playing and preserving her Chinese New Zeland family history, while also seeking to place the way they play in the broader history and diaspora of the game itself. The Book Talk with Author is co-sponsored by Purdue Graduate Student Government. ﻿ Book Discussion Thursday, November 5, 2PM-3PM AAARCC (915 5th St) Learn about the history and theory of "precarity" from Chapter 1, including examples of how Bollywood films mediate the discussions of precarious public spheres in India. Free books provided for first 5 individuals who RSVP and attend the book discussion! aaarcc.short.gy/screenrsvp​ This book is open access for Boilermakers and can be downloaded for free from: aaarcc.short.gy/precarity Book Talk with Author Thursday, November 12, 12-1 PM AAARCC (915 5th St) and virtual Join Dr. Anwer for lunch and reflection about how her book examines a filmic rendition of precarity, and how Bollywood is "not just a site of representation, but as an economic-cultural vector in its own right." Cannot join in-person? Livestream available through Microsoft Teams: aaarcc.short.gy/screenonline​ About Book & Authors Megha Anwer is a Clinical Associate Professor in the Department of English and Assistant Vice Provost for Research & Scholar Development at John Martinson Honors College. Dr. Anwer's research centers on perspectives and theories from urban studies, critical race studies, feminist studies, postcolonial studies and violence studies in a global and transnational context. Anupama Arora is a Professor of English and Communication at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth. This book explores the role that Hindi films play in how precarity is mediated by film and what that mediation reveals about both contemporary India and the social life of the movies. It examines 19 Bollywood films that constitute India’s precarious public sphere, characterized by a pervasive and profound sense of professional-personal insecurity experienced by the vast majority. Screening Precarity: Hindi Cinema and Neoliberal Crisis in Twenty-First Century India is an intervention in the politics of representation, particularly of how marginal identities are shaped, scripted and screened when neoliberalism and authoritarianism enmesh. It is also a cultural analysis of how the biggest film industry in the world is embedded in global media networks and marshals state power and star power, national histories and transnational fantasies, structural impossibilities and individual agency. ﻿Flyer: https://aaarcc.short.gy/screenflyer

events.title: Unlocking the Presidential Puzzle(s) with Mara Faccio
events.description: The Purdue University Research Center in Economics invites you to our November economic policy luncheon. Please register to join us for: Unlocking the Presidential Puzzle(s) with Mara Faccio 11:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m. Eastern Wednesday, November 11, 2026 Rawls Hall, 3rd Floor Commons 100 S. Grant Street Purdue’s West Lafayette campus Since 1927, the U.S. stock market has done substantially better under Democratic presidents than under Republicans, with the difference in annual stock market returns between the two parties averaging around 10% per year. This well-documented pattern has been dubbed the "presidential puzzle." Annual GDP growth shows a similar partisan gap. Faccio confirms this pattern using recent data. Before 1927, however, she finds that the "puzzle" reverses. Using data going back as far as 1791, she shows that annual stock market returns were almost 6% higher per year under Republican (or conservative) presidents. Annual GDP growth was 1.7% higher. Having examined competing explanations, Faccio concludes that the two opposing "puzzles" share one common source: investor risk aversion at election time. Whichever party won the election when risk aversion was high enjoyed higher subsequent returns. Mara Faccio is the Daniels School’s Tom and Patty Hefner Chair in Finance. Her primary research interests are in international finance and corporate finance. She is one of the most highly cited finance scholars. The PURCE faculty affiliate was among Stanford University and Elsevier’s top 2% of most influential scientists in the world for 2025. events.title: AI Bytes - How Much Help Is Too Much? Finding AI’s Place in Teaching and Learning
events.description: When students can turn to AI for help with everything from brainstorming to completing an assignment, it raises an important question: How much help is too much? The answer may depend less on the AI tool itself and more on what we want students to learn. How Much Help Is Too Much? Finding AI’s Place in Teaching and Learning explores how instructors can make intentional decisions about AI’s role in the learning process while helping students understand what is expected of them. Through examples and perspectives from instructors and teaching and learning experts, we’ll consider how AI can support learning objectives without replacing the critical thinking, participation, practice, and productive struggle that help students learn. We’ll also discuss the importance of transparency and clear communication, including how instructors can establish expectations around AI use and help students understand when, how, and why it may be appropriate in their coursework. Rather than starting with whether AI should or shouldn’t be used, we’ll focus on the learning we want to happen and work backward from there. Where could AI meaningfully support that learning? Where might it interfere? And how can instructors communicate those distinctions so students understand both the expectations and the reasoning behind them? Whether you’re experimenting with AI in your courses, concerned about how students are already using it, or still deciding what role it should play, you’ll leave with ideas for making intentional decisions about AI in your teaching and communicating those decisions clearly to students. events.title: Executive Forum with Winston Crawford, Senior Director of Global Ad Sales for Apple Ads
events.description: The Executive Forum is open to the public, as seating permits, and provides opportunities for the exchange of ideas and discussion of topics and issues facing business and management. Winston is the Senior Director of Global Ad Sales at Apple Ads, overseeing 700 people across 22 offices around the world responsible for driving advertising revenue across Apple Services including the App Store, Apple News and Stocks, MLS and F1 on Apple TV, Apple Maps, and Apple Podcasts. Apple Ads is the business within Apple Services that runs all of the advertising businesses within Apple’s owned and operated ecosystem. This includes the ad business within the App Store, Apple News & Stocks, Apple Maps, Apple Podcasts, and all of the advertising on Apple TV for MLS and F1. Prior to this role, Winston held the position of Senior Director of Business Management at Apple, where he led all the go-to-market functions for Apple Ads including marketing, operations, business development, business strategy, and new business initiatives. For three years in between two stints at Apple, Winston held the position of COO at Drawbridge Inc., where he played a pivotal role in the company's eventual acquisition by LinkedIn / Microsoft. As the COO of Drawbridge, Winston was responsible for all commercial efforts, including sales, business development, client strategy, and operations. Before Apple and Drawbridge, Winston held positions at Quantcast, Yahoo!, NBC Universal, General Electric, and IGN.com. Winston holds an MBA with a focus in marketing from Purdue University as well as a Bachelor of Arts from the University of Puget Sound with a major in Psychology and a minor in Philosophy. Winston grew up in Silicon Valley where he currently lives with his wife and two teenage children.

events.description: Be amazed by the power of pressure—and what it can teach us. Equal parts interactive science, comedy, and personal empowerment messages, Doktor Kaboom returns to Purdue with his new show. Doktor Kaboom: Under Pressure!illustrates physical science concepts, which are also metaphors for real-life mental and emotional pressures. Praised for keeping crowds riveted with interest and rolling with laughter, Doktor Kaboom is also known for empowering volunteers from the audience to be the heroes of the moment. In Under Pressure!, Kaboom validates the pressures some students may feel, and shares tools and life lessons as resources for dealing with the difficulties that face us all.
